notes: Concept adaptation, not a vendored copy: the pass is rewritten prose inside `pr-self-review`'s review contract, and no plugin, command, hook or skill of upstream's is installed.

History, from this repository's log: the plugin was installed on 2026-06-17 (`ponytail@ponytail` in `dot-claude/settings.json`, f206612); `pr-self-review` gained a required over-engineering lens carrying `ponytail:ponytail-review` inline on 2026-06-18 (762aa05); the pass was rewritten into the shared `code-review` skill on 2026-08-21 so it needs no plugin (f521786); the plugin and its marketplace were uninstalled on 2026-10-16 (96d500b); local `code-review` retired on 2026-11-16 and the pass moved into `pr-self-review`'s review contract, which `teammate-pr-review` also runs.

No commit was recorded when the pass was adapted. `adaptedFrom` is upstream's `main` when 762aa05 was made (2026-06-18 18:15 UTC): 91aef5d, version 4.7.0. Upstream's `skills/ponytail-review/SKILL.md` changed only in scope wording between then and the 2026-08-21 rewrite (bd6176a).
"Simplicity review" is another name for the Ponytail pass (Bryan, 2026-11-16). Bryan keeps the name Ponytail.
Upstream paths are relative to the repository root at the pinned commit.

updatePolicy.description: The pi-bots scheduled job `adapted-skill-watch` compares `commit` with upstream's head each week and, when a watched file changed since the pin, posts how many commits behind the pin is and which watched files changed. It never edits this file. Re-reading the watched files, deciding each change and advancing `commit`, `version` and `verifiedOn` is a reviewed local change.

localChanges: A review pass inside one integrated review (Standards, Spec, conditional Risk, then Ponytail last), not a plugin command or an always-on mode.
Findings use the review contract's artifact (`review-ponytail.md`), severity scale and finding gate, not upstream's own output format.
Reads the spec for outcomes, not form: a spec line that names a form Ponytail would cut is reported as over-specified.
Reports over-engineering only; correctness, security, spec conformance, coverage, naming, formatting and generic maintainability belong to the other passes.
`teammate-pr-review` runs the same pass on other people's pull requests.
acceptedUpstreamRules: The ladder, largest deletion first: `delete`, `yagni`, `reuse`, `stdlib`, `native`, then `shrink`, each with the smaller replacement shown.
Never invent deletions to look useful; a clean pass says `Lean already. Ship.`
Before reporting a cut, confirm it: the code really is unused, the helper named by `reuse` really exists.
Never propose cutting validation at a trust boundary, error handling that prevents data loss, security measures or accessibility.
The one small test or assert-based self-check that non-trivial logic needs is not bloat.
A shortcut marked with a `shortcut:` (or older `ponytail:`) comment that names its limit is a decision, not a finding, unless the expected load already crosses it.
rejectedUpstreamRules: Ponytail 5's full quality review (bug, risk, scale, missing test, speed, then lean): correctness and risk are separate passes here, so Ponytail stays narrow.

Upstream's output format (plain-English four-part findings in Must/Should/Nice groups, numbered for "fix 2 and 5", `Verdict:` and `Lean: -N lines possible.` lines): the review contract's artifacts, severity and Bryan's drafting rules own the shape.
The always-on authoring persona (`/ponytail lite|full|ultra|off`, triggering on any coding task, ending each reply with what was skipped): only the review pass is adopted.
Writing code to the ladder, comprehension-first bug fixing and leaving `shortcut:` comments in new code: rules for authoring, not review.
`merge:` and `split:` findings: duplicated code and functions mixing jobs belong to Standards.
"Never cut anything the user asked for": here a spec that names a form Ponytail would cut is reported as over-specified.
Plugin, marketplace, hook, status-line and per-harness installs: the pass needs none.

changes.change: Scope wording: over-engineering and complexity only; correctness, security and performance go to a normal review.
changes.reason: Already the local rule ("Ponytail does not report correctness, security..."); no edit.

changes.change: A `reuse:` tag: an equivalent helper already in the repository; name the path.
changes.reason: Re-implementing what already lives a few files away is common over-engineering the five old tags missed. Added to the ladder.

changes.change: Number findings across the report so the user can say "fix 2 and 5".
changes.reason: Findings here go to the acceptance owner for disposition and into `integrated-review.json`, not to Bryan to pick by number.

changes.change: Ponytail 5: the review becomes a full quality review (bug, risk, scale, missing test, speed, lean), reading callers and the expected load.
changes.reason: Standards, Spec and Risk already cover correctness and risk as separate passes; folding them into Ponytail would duplicate them and break the narrow pass the contract and its tests require.

changes.change: Check before you report: every finding needs a concrete case; re-read the lines and confirm the code really is unused.
changes.reason: Guards against cutting code that is in use or naming a helper that doesn't exist. One sentence added.

changes.change: Plain-English output, four-part findings in Must/Should/Nice groups, `Verdict:`; `Lean already. Ship.` becomes `Looks good. Ship.` and `net:` becomes `Lean: -N lines possible.`
changes.reason: The artifact shape, severity scale and clean-summary string are load-bearing for `ship`, the lane-reviewer agents and tests; Bryan's drafting rules own the human-facing text.

changes.change: New `merge:` (near-copies) and `split:` (a function doing unrelated jobs) lean findings.
changes.reason: Duplicated code and divergent change are Standards smells here; Ponytail stays on what to cut.

changes.change: A shortcut marked `shortcut:` (or older `ponytail:`) that names its limit is a decision, not a finding, unless the load already crosses it.
changes.reason: A deliberate, documented shortcut is the kind of simplicity Ponytail wants; flagging it is noise. One sentence added.

changes.change: Trigger the persona on any coding task, not only on keywords.
changes.reason: The always-on authoring persona is not adopted; only the review pass is.

changes.change: A reuse rung (already in this codebase) on the ladder; understand the problem before climbing it; bug fixes go to the root cause.
changes.reason: Reuse rung accepted as the `reuse` tag. Comprehension-first and root-cause fixing are authoring rules for correctness and are rejected for this pass.

changes.change: Use the `ponytail:` marker only for real corner-cuts with a known ceiling.
changes.reason: An authoring rule for writing markers; the review side is covered by the accepted shortcut-marker rule.

changes.change: Ponytail 5 rules: the smallest complete change, keep the codebase's structure, comment only the why, one small check for non-trivial logic, and never cut validation at trust boundaries, data-loss error handling, security, accessibility, hardware calibration or anything the user asked for.
changes.reason: Accepted for review: never propose cutting validation, data-loss error handling, security or accessibility, and the one small check for non-trivial logic is not bloat. Rejected: the authoring rules, and "anything the user asked for", which the local over-specified-spec rule overrides.

changes.change: New code uses a neutral `shortcut:` comment marker instead of `ponytail:`.
changes.reason: Accepted only as recognising both markers in review (above); the pass writes no code.

changes.change: An `off` level in the argument hint.
changes.reason: Levels belong to the persona, which is not adopted.
